checks.finding: requirements.md carries a dedicated Field Definitions section (guard-runtime surface, tool_name shape, PATH-restricted subshell, decision parity, combined suite, human-copy staging, preventive restructuring) and every Goal/AC enumerates its closed sets explicitly (e.g. the 5 PATH-availability branches + 1 precedence case for REQ-001; the 4 runtimes x 3 tool_name shapes for REQ-002; the exact greenfield|brownfield closed set for REQ-003). No term, actor, state, input, or output was found materially under-specified.

requirements.md's 'Re-verification note' (the paragraph beginning 'Everything else investigation.md asserts was re-confirmed byte-identical at re-verification time') lists, without any 'superseded'/'historical-only' qualifier attached to this specific clause, both 'ADR-0010's `Status: Proposed(人間承認待ち)`' and '`tests/workflow-scenarios/` still does not exist' as re-confirmed current facts, presented in the same undifferentiated sentence as genuinely-still-true facts (e.g. PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES membership, the sdd-hook-guard.sh fallback chain). This directly conflicts with the 'Stream C status record (authoritative)' section that immediately follows it: 'ADR-0010 reached `Status: Accepted`... Stream C's implementation then landed inside this feature: T-004 authored `tests/workflow-scenarios/` and `workflow-scenarios.tests.sh`.' The document's own reconciliation promise ('Every passage below that once carried an operative Blocked pending ADR-0010 instruction has been reconciled to this record in place') only covers passages structurally below the Stream C status record; the Re-verification note sits above it and is left unreconciled. The Assumptions section later relabels the ADR-0010-Proposed sub-claim as 'an authoring-time snapshot, not a current-state claim,' but no passage anywhere relabels the 'tests/workflow-scenarios/ still does not exist' sub-claim, so that specific factual conflict is never resolved in the document. Downstream failure mode: a task-decomposition or implementation-policy reviewer who reads the prominent, detailed Re-verification note before reaching the later Stream C status record/Main Workflows/AC-012..015 sections would reasonably conclude tests/workflow-scenarios/ does not exist and ADR-0010 is still Proposed, directly contradicting the rest of the document's operative treatment of Stream C as unblocked and landed -- the exact 'Stream C blocked vs. unblocked' ambiguity class that produced three consecutive BLOCKED verdicts in attempt 3, recurring here because this passage's phrasing ('still does not exist', a quoted 'Status: Proposed' value) falls outside the blocker/blocked/unblock/is accepted/until then/not yet keyword sweep used for the round-4 reconciliation. This belongs to spec review because it is a document-internal factual conflict about current project state that a design or task reviewer cannot resolve without guessing which of the two contradicting passages is authoritative.

acceptance-tests.md and requirements.md's Edge Cases section cover the material negative/boundary/failure paths implied by the Goals: fail-closed deny_unavailable across both emit modes (AC-005/TEST-005), an explicit cross-runtime decision-parity divergence check (AC-011/TEST-011), a dedicated false-DENY control sub-case for the substring-collision defect (AC-010, '1 control sub-case proving the numeric substring alone ... never triggers a false DENY'), a literal RED-then-GREEN self-check proving the CI lane-marking self-check can catch a dropped step (AC-017/TEST-017), and named-reason SKIP handling when a host lacks an interpreter (TEST-008..011 notes) rather than a silent pass.

The dedicated Assumptions section enumerates 5 explicit, individually-scoped assumptions (registration-gap state, PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES/PHASE2_HUMAN_COPY_TARGETS membership, identity-ledger tail, ADR-0010 status, loop-driver.sh stage scope, collection-layer.tests.sh technique), each carrying an explicit RE-VERIFY-at-implementation-time instruction (WFI-013 discipline) rather than being silently presumed resolved -- none is left as an unmarked, unresolved assumption.

Human approval/governance boundaries are concretely testable: the R-10-protected CI workflow may only be changed via staged human-copy candidates under `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/` plus `MANIFEST.sha256`, verified by AC-016/017/020's self-checks against the staged candidate vs. the live file (Roles and Permissions; Security Boundaries B3); and ADR-0010's Accepted decision is explicitly attributed to the human maintainer, not any agent session ('that decision was NOT made by this spec or by any agent session, and it has since been made (commit 67015a5)'), giving the irreversible-change/governance boundary an explicit, checkable owner and mechanism.

Beyond the single contradiction already captured under CONTRADICTION, the specification supplies concrete file:line-anchored targets, Roles and Permissions, a Security Boundaries trust-boundary table, and per-stream Main Workflows detail sufficient for an implementation-policy/design reviewer to proceed without inventing missing product behavior.

Skipped: no `domain/` directory, `Bounded-Context:` field, or domain-contract reference appears anywhere in requirements.md, acceptance-tests.md, or investigation.md -- the skip condition (domain/ absent or its Approved-status contract not evidenced) applies.
